mechanism: The same avatar and lip-sync models are sold through two doors: a metered API and a flat-credit web app. The web app bills per credit bundle, so a minute of finished video costs roughly a third as much, but it needs a person at a browser instead of a script. idea_why: Routing drafts through the cheap manual door and finals through the API is ordinary cost arbitrage between two prices for the same output.
breakdown: List each video job and tag it draft or final. Draft jobs go through the web app free or credit tier, with a person pasting the script and downloading the render. missing: Nobody has a measured per-minute cost table for both routes on a real job.

mechanism: The agent first watches a low-frame-rate preview, then writes a Context, Focus, Points plan listing what to look for and which tool to use. It revisits chosen time segments with tools, updates the plan, and writes one caption. It is trained with GRPO using rewards for key facts, plan alignment and a penalty for useless tool calls.
claim: Reviso beats open-source baselines on four video captioning benchmarks and improves downstream video QA.
why_not_testable: Needs trained model weights and a GPU, and no local model is installed.
one_line: A video captioner that plans what to look at from a quick preview, then revisits only the key moments.
idea_why: Coarse pass then targeted re-inspection is a standard cost-saving pattern for any long input.
breakdown: The pattern can be copied without the training: sample frames sparsely, ask a model for a short plan of what matters, then pull full-rate frames only for those segments. That would sit on top of the transcript pipeline and ffmpeg. Training the RL policy is a research job no script covers.
